titulo: The routine: reflexive verbs, frequency and -ir verbs: Reflexive verbs

aula.titulo: The routine: reflexive verbs, frequency and -ir verbs
aula.objetivo: Talk about your daily routine with reflexive verbs, say how often you do things, and conjugate regular -ir verbs.

blocos.titulo: Se lever, se coucher: reflexive verbs
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: reflexive verbs take a pronoun that repeats the subject: «je me lève», «tu te lèves», «il/elle/on se lève», «nous nous levons», «vous vous levez», «ils/elles se lèvent». STEP 2: before a vowel or silent «h», «me», «te» and «se» become «m'», «t'» and «s'»: «je m'habille», «il s'appelle». STEP 3: «se lever» changes its spelling: «je lève, tu lèves, il lève, ils lèvent», but «nous levons, vous levez» (the «è» disappears). «Se promener» does the same: «je me promène». STEP 4: in the negative, the pronoun comes after «ne»: «Je ne me lève pas tôt.» STEP 5: in an informal question: «Tu te lèves à quelle heure ?» STEP 6: in the near future, the pronoun goes before the infinitive: «Je vais me coucher.» STEP 7: many reflexive verbs are actions done to your own body (se laver, s'habiller) or changes of state (se lever, se coucher). English rarely uses the pronoun («myself»): «I get up», but also «I wash my hands».
blocos.comparacao: English has few reflexive verbs, like «to wash oneself» or «to enjoy oneself», and uses the pronoun less. In French, many everyday verbs always need the pronoun («se lever»), even when English has none: «to wake up» = «se réveiller».

linhas.example: Je me lève à sept heures.
Vous vous levez à huit heures.
Ils se lèvent à six heures.

erros.certo: Je me lève à sept heures.

erros.errado: Je ne lève pas me tôt.
erros.certo: Je ne me lève pas tôt.

blocos.enunciado: Describe your morning routine with six reflexive verbs: «Je me réveille à… Je me lève à… Je me lave… Je m'habille…»
Say out loud what you are going to do tomorrow and how you will get to work or school.
